extraction.name: OpenBookQA
extraction.description: A new kind of question answering dataset modeled after open book exams for assessing human understanding of a subject. It consists of 5957 multiple-choice questions and a set of 1326 diverse facts about elementary level science. The questions probe an understanding of these facts and their application to novel situations, requiring multi-hop reasoning with broad common knowledge.
extraction.creator: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal
extraction.publisher: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Seattle, WA, U.S.A. and Research Training Group AIPHES & Heidelberg University, Heidelberg, Germany
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A multi-stage process starting with a set of core science facts, using crowd-sourcing to generate questions based on these facts that probe novel situations, using an automatic filter to ensure hardness for retrieval and association based systems, using a crowd filter to ensure answerability by a lay person, and further using an expert filter to ensure higher quality in Dev and Test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The core science facts are a subset of the WorldTree corpus (Jansen et al., 2018), filtered down to 1326 facts that appear general enough to be applicable to multiple situations from the 2287 facts marked as 'central'.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The system verifies questions pass basic checks such as exactly 4 answer choices, no negation words to trivially fool baselines, and uniform answer choice length. The answer choices are randomly shuffled to avoid unintended bias.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A crowd-worker is shown a random science fact and asked to think of a second common fact to derive a new assertion. The worker converts this into a 4-way multiple choice question. The question is fed to an IR solver and word association solver to verify hardness. It is then shown to 5 new crowd-workers to answer. If at least 4 out of 5 workers answer correctly, it is deemed answerable and kept.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were evaluated for answerability by requiring at least 4 out of 5 crowd-workers to answer correctly. The Dev and Test splits were further filtered by an in-house expert to ensure higher quality.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers from North America and with a 'masters' level qualification.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Information retrieval solver (Clark et al., 2016) and a word association based solver (Turney, 2017) used for automatic filtering.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human bias in crowdsourced datasets arising from the difficulty of creating good quality incorrect answers. Incorrect answers often tend to be homogeneous or share common properties (e.g., non-scientific terms) uncharacteristic of the correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The authored additional facts (K) tend to be noisy (incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related). Models trained on the Train set may not perform well on distant domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation (Dev), and Testing. For each Train and Dev question, the dataset includes the core fact as an intermediate supervision signal.
